scope.description: A Raft node whose Transport implements the heartbeat fast path, receiving a pure AppendEntries heartbeat from a peer whose RPCHeader.ProtocolVersion is outside the window checkRPCHeader accepts. The obligation concerns the guard applied to that entry path, not the concurrency of the handler or the content of the heartbeat.
assumptions: The transport classifies the request as a heartbeat exactly as net_transport does: Term != 0, a leader address present, PrevLogEntry/PrevLogTerm zero, no entries and LeaderCommitIndex zero.
checkRPCHeader is the authoritative protocol-version gate for AppendEntries on the normal path.
excluded: Whether the handler's concurrent execution is safe is a separate question; here it only touches lock- or atomic-protected fields.
Log safety is out of scope: this path carries no entries, prev-log fields or commit index.

properties.reason: Independent applicability, correlated prerequisites and fully observed result comparison

adaptations: The heartbeat is delivered by invoking processHeartbeat directly. That is the body of the handler installed by transport.SetHeartbeatHandler, and the package's own integration test demonstrates the callback contract by calling r.processHeartbeat(rpc) from inside a custom heartbeat handler; net_transport's fast path is reached only over TCP and network access is disabled in the execution sandbox, so the transport classification is declared as a sourced premise instead of being reproduced.
Nodes are constructed with conf.skipStartup = true, the pattern used by the package's own tests, so no background goroutines run and the request handlers can be driven without racing the main loop.
No protocol logic is modified: the harness only constructs requests and reads existing state accessors.

plan_uncertainties: Reachability of an out-of-window peer that can produce a pure heartbeat in a legal deployment.
Whether the guard omission is deliberate design, making the correct disposition a documented assumption rather than a violation.
The election consequence of refreshing last contact on this path is not measured.
grounding_unresolved: Reachability of the fast path with an out-of-window peer.
Whether the omission is deliberate design.

Whether a peer outside the supported protocol window can deliver a pure heartbeat in a legal deployment is a premise about peers, not about this node; it is declared by the scenario and not exercised end to end.
The consequence on elections (whether repeated refreshes of last contact suffice to suppress this node's own election) is not measured here.

blockers: Open review issue c5b1dc9500994c069cfd0362d39da853 [S40,S41,S42,S43,S16,S14]: processHeartbeat's own comment says it must only be called from the main thread, while the transport invokes it from a connection goroutine; that comment discrepancy is not the subject here but reduces confidence that the fast path's guard requirements were reasoned through.
